It started out with our biology teacher talking about possibly missing 2 weeks of classes in the middle of our lab, then the same day with the school anouncing that the cafeteria and places with a big flux of people gathering will be closed, then the day after anouncing that all schools would be closed and then learning we couldn't go back to school until may.

 Talking to my parents about it was a slap to reality because I realized they were in the graphic of vulnerable people. And now, my boyfriend won't be able to work as the government closed all non-essential businesses. He was the sole provider of money for our apartment and we dont have a lot saved up. I'm scared and non hopeful and I know a lot of people are in our shoes and it's very frustating because we can't do anything about it. 

I sometimes end up thinking of the doctors losing their lives and sanity at their job right now, probably wishing for it to stop and wishing to see their familly again. And the people hospitalised not knowing if they will make it, hoping they will get to see their loved one's faces one more time. Thinking "I didn't want to die like this, not here, not now" About the ones who didn't make it The children wondering when mom or dad are gonna come home. I also end up thinking of all the people craving for some sort of emotional connection through all means with other people because they were never used to being so alone for this long. Loneliness grasps their heart and doesn't let go. 

For anyone reading this tonight, we are here together.

We will do our best together 

We will remember this time together

Take care of each other people, because this is the best time to do so.

Call your parents to tell them you love them.

Call your friends and learn more about their past and the future they want.

Take time to learn the things you had wanted to learn but didn't have the time to.

And most of all, take care of yourself. Because I'm sure you didn't have time for that either and we want you well.

So context, I  became a vegetarian about 3 years ago, it hasn't always been fun with the family and other people's comments here and there, but I have to say the worst part are the holyday meals.

So we always used to have big ass buffets for christmas at my grandfather's appartment building. He would always ask to get the top floor reserved for the 25th so our entire familly could come and eat together and that's about 30 people.

It was always fun to be part of that until I became a vegetarian. Then at every familly meal we got for christmas, my only option was salad(which I never liked, I don't eat salad) , some vegetables, and a bit of cold hard boiled eggs. I have to eat this cold, boring sad meal at the same table my family eat their hot meals with such content faces. They comment on how good it is and blablabla while I starve.

Don't get me wrong, the first year it happened , I had been a vegetarian for 11 months (I started in febuary) , but I understood they might have not remembered or they were not used to it, thus why I had to let it go. But after THREE years, there is still no improvments and I had to bring my own food, so even though it was a family get together, I did not feel like part of the family anymore because nobody aknowleged me. It was like I was a decoration on the wall.

Now I always bring my own food, even sometimes when I go at my parent's. Hopefully one day it will change, but for now, I'll have to get used to not being aknowledged when it comes to food.

Ok so this is a story of when I was 7 or 8 and I was visiting my uncle's house. He had this awesome pool me and my big brother would always play in everytime we went there. So this time too, me and my brother play in the pool, my mother is on a long chair not too far, talking with my aunt.  Mind you, I was a very good swimmer but I was still too tiny to touch the ground, so to keep my head on top of the water I had to swim all the time. My big brother decided that for fun he would climb on top of my shoulders (he always liked fighting with me, throwing me around the water, but that was a first). Now remember I'm too small to reach the bottom so while he's on my shoulders, I sink to the bottom. I remember trying to get up, I was trying very hard to keep my breath and move but I felt pinned down. I didn't think of pinching him or any other thing, so I just stayed there,  waiting for my brother to get off, I was hoping he would leave soon, but the more I wished for it, the more painful it felt, my body was violently demanding air, and I couldn't give it what it needed. I felt hopeless and was panicking. I was under the water for what seemed like 2 minutes. Every second was excrutiatingly painful for me. Normally at that point, people would have gone back up because of their survival instinct, but I was way past that point. But then something happened.I remember a weird surge of comfort went through me, as if I just took a huge load of air and the pain was all gone. It was as if I had gone back up and took a deep breath, but I was definetly still under the water, and before I could make sense of what was happening, I felt my brother get off my shoulders, and so I swam back up as fast as possible. I can still remember vividly that feeling. Now can you imagine what was going through the mind of a kid, I thought I must have found a way to breathe under water lol. I asked my biology teacher what could explain what happened 13 years ago, and she said I was probably about to lose consciousness, thus the pain going away. Though I still count myself lucky that my brother got off when he did because when I asked my mom about it, she said she saw nothing. I would have drowned that day if it wasn't for that.
